He took the Testimony and put it into the Ark, set the poles on the Ark, and placed the cover on top of the Ark. He brought the Ark into the Tabernacle, hung the curtain of the screen, and screened the Ark of the Testimony, as Hashem had commanded Moses. He put the table in the Tent of Meeting, on the north side of the Tabernacle, outside the curtain, and set the bread in order upon it before Hashem, as Hashem had commanded Moses. He set the menorah in the Tent of Meeting, opposite the table, on the south side of the Tabernacle, and lit the lamps before Hashem, as Hashem had commanded Moses. He set the golden altar in the Tent of Meeting before the curtain, and burned fragrant incense upon it, as Hashem had commanded Moses. He put up the screen at the entrance of the Tabernacle. He set the altar of burnt offering at the entrance of the Tabernacle of the Tent of Meeting, and offered upon it the burnt offering and the meal offering, as Hashem had commanded Moses. He set the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar, and put water there for washing. Moses and Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet from it; when they entered the Tent of Meeting, and when they approached the altar, they washed, as Hashem had commanded Moses. He set up the court around the Tabernacle and the altar, and hung the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work. Then the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and the glory of Hashem filled the Tabernacle. Moses could not enter the Tent of Meeting, because the cloud rested upon it, and the glory of Hashem filled the Tabernacle. When the cloud lifted from over the Tabernacle, the children of Israel would set out on all their journeys; but if the cloud did not lift, they would not set out until the day it lifted. For the cloud of Hashem was upon the Tabernacle by day, and fire was in it by night, in the sight of all the House of Israel, in all their journeys.

Hashem spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: Thus shall you bless the children of Israel; say to them: May Hashem bless you and keep you. May Hashem make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you. May Hashem lift up His face toward you and grant you peace. So shall they place My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them.

On the day that Moses finished setting up the Tabernacle, he anointed it and sanctified it, with all its furnishings and the altar with all its utensils; he anointed them and sanctified them. The princes of Israel, the heads of their fathers’ houses, who were the princes of the tribes and stood over those who were counted, made their offerings. They brought their offering before Hashem: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for every two princes and an ox for each one; and they presented them before the Tabernacle. Hashem said to Moses: Take these from them, that they may be used in the service of the Tent of Meeting, and give them to the Levites, to each man according to his service. So Moses took the wagons and the oxen and gave them to the Levites. Two wagons and four oxen he gave to the sons of Gershon, according to their service; and four wagons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to their service, under the direction of Ithamar son of Aaron the priest. But to the sons of Kohath he gave none, because theirs was the service of the holy things, which they carried on their shoulders. The princes brought the dedication offering for the altar on the day it was anointed; the princes presented their offering before the altar. And Hashem said to Moses: One prince each day, one prince each day, shall present his offering for the dedication of the altar.

The one who presented his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Nahshon son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah, which is sealed with Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

Just as in this month You redeemed Your people, the tribes of Your inheritance, from the iron furnace, from Egypt, and remembered with love, for praise, for fame, and for glory, the names of the tribes of their fathers, for the miracles, the deliverance, the mighty acts, and the salvations that You wrought with them, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, may You mercifully visit Your flock, and remember for us the love of the early tribes of Yah, in this present exile. The tribe of Judah is in distress and sorrow. And just as they gave thanks to Hashem for His kindness at the going out from Egypt in the merit of Judah, so may we give thanks to You, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, for our redemption and for the deliverance of our souls, in the merit of Judah, king among his brothers. The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor the ruler’s staff from between his feet. His seed shall endure forever, and his throne like the sun before You. May our eyes behold the king in his beauty, and may our heart rejoice. And may You reign, You, Hashem our God, speedily over all Your works, on Mount Zion, the dwelling place of Your glory, and in Jerusalem, Your holy city, as it is written in Your holy words: “Hashem shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation. Halleluyah!” And it is said: “For the kingship is Hashem’s, and He rules over the nations.” “Saviors shall go up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingship shall be Hashem’s.” “Hashem shall be King over all the earth; on that day Hashem shall be One and His name One.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. Receive our cry and hear our outcry, You who know what is hidden.

The word of Hashem came to me, saying: And you, son of man, take one stick and write on it, “For Judah and for the children of Israel his companions”; and take another stick and write on it, “For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and all the House of Israel his companions.” Join them one to the other into one stick, so that they become one in your hand. And when your people say to you, “Will you not tell us what you mean by these?” say to them: Thus says Hashem God: Behold, I am taking the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions, and I will put them together with the stick of Judah and make them one stick, and they shall be one in My hand. The sticks on which you write shall be in your hand, before their eyes. Then say to them: Thus says Hashem God: Behold, I am taking the children of Israel from among the nations where they have gone, and I will gather them from all around and bring them to their own land. I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king over them all; they shall no longer be two nations, and no longer be divided into two kingdoms. They shall no longer defile themselves with their idols and their detestable things, or with any of their transgressions. I will save them from all their dwelling places in which they sinned, and I will cleanse them; they shall be My people, and I will be their God. My servant David shall be king over them, and they shall all have one shepherd. They shall follow My laws and keep My statutes and observe them. They shall dwell in the land that I gave to My servant Jacob, in which your fathers dwelt; they shall dwell in it, they and their children and their children’s children, forever; and David My servant shall be their prince forever. I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them. I will establish them and multiply them, and I will set My sanctuary among them forever. My dwelling place shall be with them; I will be their God, and they shall be My people. Then the nations shall know that I am Hashem who sanctifies Israel, when My sanctuary is among them forever.

A Song of Ascents, of David. I rejoiced when they said to me, “Let us go to the House of Hashem.” Our feet were standing within your gates, Jerusalem. Jerusalem, built as a city that is joined together, to which the tribes go up, the tribes of Yah, as a testimony for Israel, to give thanks to the name of Hashem. For there the thrones of judgment were set, the thrones of the House of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem: may those who love you be at peace. May there be peace within your walls, tranquility within your palaces. For the sake of my brothers and my friends, I will say, “Peace be within you.” For the sake of the House of Hashem our God, I will seek your good.

“Every man by his standard, with the signs” (Numbers 2:2). These are the four camps of the Community of Israel, which are the twelve tribes, the twelve boundaries, all around her. All is like the pattern above. It is written: “Where the tribes went up, the tribes of Yah, and so on.” “Where the tribes went up” — these are the twelve tribes, the twelve boundaries below.

“The tribes of Yah” — they have already explained this: because of the Yod-Heh, “a testimony for Israel,” surely. And therefore “the Reubenite, the Simeonite” — Yod-Heh is in each and every one. But surely it is so, for the supernal holy Tree sealed them with its seal. And they explained, as it is written: “And the likeness of their faces: the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side, and so on.” The image of Man is included in all of them, and the faces were toward the four directions of the world, and they are divided in their images, and all of them are included in him, in Man.

Michael on the right, Gabriel on the left, Uriel in front of them, Raphael behind them, and the Presence above them. Two on this side, two on that side, and she in the middle. In the same way on the earth below: two on this side, two on that side, and Yod-Heh between them.

When two standards journey, what is written? “Then the Tent of Meeting shall set out, the camp of the Levites, and so on.” And afterward, those other two. They are four camps, for the four directions of the world, and twelve are found. So too below, like the pattern above. “And the standard of the camp of Judah set out first” — opposite the camp of Uriel; and the camp of Reuben opposite the camp of Michael. This is for the south and this for the east. The altar likewise: south-east. And the camp of Dan to the north; the camp of Ephraim, west. The camp of Dan opposite the camp of Gabriel; the camp of Ephraim to the west, opposite the camp of Raphael. The altar likewise: north-west. Everything is joined, one to the other, until everything ascends and is united in the holy Name, which is the beginning of everything, the highest of everything, the holiest of everything. Everything is included in it. Yod, the east, is the beginning of light; it goes and roams and brings forth to the south. And the south goes out and depends on the beginning of the east. Heh is the south; from it the south in the world goes out. And Yod enters into the beginning of the east, and brings it forth.

And from Heh depend south and north, and that which is between them, Yod, east. Yod, east; Yod-Heh, south and north depend on it. Vav is in the middle, and this is the “male son.” Therefore he is between north and south. And on this we learned: whoever places his bed between north and south will have male sons, for this male son is between north and south. The upper Heh, on which depend north and south, with the male son between them, in the secret of Yod-Vav-Heh. The last Heh is the west.

And therefore the south is attached to the east, which is the beginning of the sun, and depends on it. And on this we learned: from the side of the Father, supernal Kindness is attached and depends; from the side of the Mother, Strength depends. In the same way, everything is attached, one to the other.

The corners of the altar likewise revolve, and he comes to the south-east corner. For the south has its strength in the east, which is the beginning of the sun, and the strength of the sun rests only at its beginning. East-north: since the south takes its strength from the east, it illuminates the north, and the north is included in the south, for the left is included in the right.

North-west, for the west, which is in the last Heh, takes from the north. And therefore the north goes to the west. West-south: she goes to join with the south, just as the south depends on the east, and its strength goes at the beginning. So too the west goes to be united with the south. This is what is written: “and his right hand embraces me.” The right hand is the south. For this reason she is nursed from two sides, from the north and from the south. This is what is written: “His left hand is under my head, and his right hand embraces me.” “His left hand” is the north, and “his right hand” is the south.

And this secret we learned: the Holy One, blessed be He, places His bed between north and south, and He holds this son, surely. And therefore people should place their beds between north and south. “And so my father taught me”: that male children will be given to them. For he is directed toward the perfect, supernal faith, in the completeness of everything, toward the Holy One, blessed be He, who is between north and south, and toward the Community of Israel, who shine between north and south. Surely they will have male children.

And in everything one must show action like the pattern above; and as an action is shown below, so it is aroused above, and they have explained this. Rabbi Pinchas heard, kissed Rabbi Elazar, wept, and smiled, and said: Happy is my portion in this world and in the world to come.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that today You shine, in Your great kindness, upon the holy souls standing in the three rows in Eden, who chirp with their voices like birds, “and every soul shall praise Yah,” to extol and glorify the splendor of Your name, our King, and who offer entreaty for life and peace for us, the children of Your friends. Please, in the power of the greatness of Your mercy, let Your ears be attentive to them, and turn to their prayer with mercy, to cancel from us and from all the House of Israel all burning anger, every kind of destroyer, and every kind of calamity. May You lengthen our days in good and our years in pleasantness: lives of peace, lives of tranquility, lives of goodness, lives of blessing, lives of good livelihood, lives of strength in the bones, lives in which there is fear of sin, lives in which there is no shame or disgrace, lives of wealth and honor for Your service, lives in which we have love of Torah for its own sake, lives in which You fulfill all the wishes of our heart for good.

And may Your kindness be upon these holy souls, and may their good memory ascend and come, reach, be seen and favored, be heard, recalled, and remembered, before Your glorious throne, “and may they find rest.” Bind their souls before You and within, to the holy place — “no eye has seen, God, besides You” — and satisfy their souls with radiance; “they are sated from the abundance of Your house, and You give them to drink from the stream of Your delights.” Set our portion with them, and may we merit, live, and inherit goodness and blessing in the life of the World to Come. And those souls that are cast out and flutter in the air of the world, and those who died before their time and were not handed over to Dumah, and those buried in the earth who “shall blossom from the city like the grass of the earth,” who have not yet gained the strength to come to their rest — You, God, who give light to the earth and to those who dwell on it with mercy, make Your face shine and cover their iniquity and transgression, and say to the angel appointed over them to lighten their judgment, their sentence, and their burden. May Hashem grant them that they find a secure rest, each one at his own camp, in the rest of peace, quiet, and security forever, and “in the shadow of the Almighty may they lodge,” under the wings of the cherubim; from level to level and from rung to rung may they arise and ascend. And whoever has no merits with which to ascend, deal with him with kindness, a gift freely given, as it is said: “And He said: I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of Hashem before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will show mercy to whom I will show mercy.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer.

On the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, presented his offering. He presented as his offering one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Nethanel son of Zuar, of the tribe of Issachar, which is sealed with the attribute of Eternity of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

Just as in this month You redeemed Your people, the tribes of Your inheritance, from the iron furnace, from Egypt, and remembered with love, for praise, for fame, and for glory, the names of the tribes of their fathers, for the miracles, the deliverance, the mighty acts, and the salvations that You wrought with them, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, may You mercifully visit Your flock, and remember for us the love of the early tribes of Yah, in this present exile. And just as You increased the reward of our fathers in these days, at this time, in the merit of Issachar — “and afterward they shall go out with great wealth” — so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, set the reward of Your people, afflicted and battered in this present exile, and give a good reward to all who trust in Your name in truth, so that we are never ashamed, for in You we have trusted, and for Your salvation we have hoped all day long, in the merit of Issachar and his blessing: “He saw that rest was good, and the land that it was pleasant.” “Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed times; let your eyes see Jerusalem, a peaceful abode, a tent that shall not be moved, whose stakes shall never be pulled up, and none of whose cords shall be broken, Hashem of hosts.” Make Your face shine, that we may be saved. Bless them, purify them; Your righteous mercies grant them always. May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the third day, the prince of the children of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Eliab son of Helon, of the tribe of Zebulun, which is sealed with the attribute of Splendor of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You redeemed our fathers from Egypt and caused Your Presence to dwell among them in the House of Zebul, in the merit of Zebulun, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, “remember Your congregation, which You acquired long ago,” in this present exile, bitter and hasty. And in the merit of Zebulun, return Your Presence to the House of Zebul, the glory of Your splendor. May You dwell within Jerusalem, Your city, as You have spoken, and speedily establish the throne of David within it. Attend to this vine, which is ailing, all day long, and show us splendor for good. “Save us, Hashem our God, and gather us from among the nations, to give thanks to Your holy name and to glory in Your praise.” And establish for Your servants the blessing of Zebulun: “Peoples shall call to the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they shall draw from the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.” “Hashem of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah.” Almighty, Holy One, in Your great goodness lead Your congregation. May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the fourth day, the prince of the children of Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Elizur son of Shedeur, of the tribe of Reuben, which is sealed with the attribute of Kindness of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You saw the affliction of Your people, the flock of Your pasture, Israel, in Egypt in these days, at this time, in the merit of Reuben, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, in this present exile, “look and see our disgrace.” And in the merit of Reuben, “see our affliction, plead our cause,” and speedily redeem us with a complete redemption. Please, by the power of the greatness of Your right hand, release the bound. “Arise, be our help, and redeem us for the sake of Your kindness.” “Show Your wondrous kindnesses, You who save those who take refuge from their adversaries by Your right hand.” “May Your kindness, Hashem, be upon us, as we have hoped in You.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the fifth day, the prince of the children of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, of the tribe of Simeon, which is sealed with the attribute of Strength of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You heard the groaning of the children of Israel, Your people, in Egypt in these days, at this time, in the merit of Simeon, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, visit us with a visitation of salvation and mercy in this bitter and hasty exile. And in the merit of Simeon, accept the song of Your people; raise us up, purify us, Awesome One. Hear our voice and accept with mercy and with favor our prayer, we who groan from the pit of exile and from the land of captivity. God, look: our honor is humbled among the nations, and they treat us as impure as a menstruating woman. How long will Your strength be in captivity, and Your glory in the hand of the oppressor? They will see and be ashamed, and be dismayed at their own might. Rouse Your might and save us, for Your name’s sake. “Hashem goes out like a mighty man, like a man of war He rouses His zeal; He shouts, yes, He roars, He prevails over His enemies.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the sixth day, the prince of the children of Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Deuel.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Eliasaph son of Deuel, of the tribe of Gad, which is sealed with the attribute of Splendor of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as when Israel went out from Egypt You made the manna descend for them from the heavens of Your heights, and it was like coriander seed, in the merit of Gad, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, “Mighty, Holy One, in Your great goodness lead Your congregation,” in this present exile, open for us the treasuries of the supernal, white dew, from the two constellations, “preserving” and “clearing,” the way of the palate and the throat, to Abba and Imma, and from Abba and Imma to the Lesser Countenance, and from the Lesser Countenance to the Field of Holy Apples, from where supernal sustenance is given, from the mills that grind manna there for the righteous. And satisfy the whole world with Your goodness, and give dew and rain for blessing upon the whole face of the earth, “from the bounty of heaven, from the dew, and from the deep that lies beneath.” And in the merit of Gad, sealed at the heel of the splendor of Your kingship, “I will be like the dew to Israel; he shall blossom like the lily and strike his roots like Lebanon. His shoots shall spread, and his beauty shall be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Lebanon.” And in Your salvation, our King, raise up and lift the horn of Messiah son of David, Your servant, and place some of Your splendor upon him. “His glory is great through Your salvation; splendor and majesty You lay upon him.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the seventh day, the prince of the children of Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Elishama son of Ammihud, of the tribe of Ephraim, which is sealed with the crown of Foundation of the Lesser Countenance (Z’eir Anpin), his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children. Unique and Exalted One, turn to Your people, who remember Your holiness. “Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, rouse Your might and come to save us.” And speedily establish the throne of kingship of Messiah son of Ephraim within Jerusalem, and let there be no distress or grief in our redemption, that Messiah son of Ephraim not be killed, who will begin to comfort us and to raise our banner over the nations at the hands of the wicked Armilus. “He asked life of You; You gave it to him, length of days forever and ever.” As with his blessing, so bless him: “His firstborn bull, majesty is his, and his horns are the horns of the wild ox; with them he shall gore the peoples, all together, to the ends of the earth. These are the myriads of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.”

And in the merit of Ephraim, sealed with the crown of Foundation of the Lesser Countenance: “Remember, Hashem, against the Edomites the day of Jerusalem, who said, ‘Strip her, strip her, down to her foundation!’” “And all the horns of the wicked I will cut off; the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up.” “For You, Hashem, bless the righteous; You surround him with favor as with a shield.” “You will arise and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to favor her, for the appointed time has come.” And He who redeemed the fathers when Israel went out from Egypt — may Hashem again redeem the sons a second time. “Let Israel rejoice in his Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.” “The envy of Ephraim shall depart, and those who harass Judah shall be cut off; Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not harass Ephraim.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the eighth day, the prince of the children of Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, of the tribe of Manasseh, which is sealed with the aspect of Foundation, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You lifted all their toil from Israel and removed the burden from their shoulders in Egypt in these days, at this time, in the merit of Manasseh, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, You, Hashem, will not forget us in this present exile. See that Your people, this great nation, is not like one forgotten in the land of oblivion, and bring our soul out of confinement to give thanks to Your name. And therefore we put our hope in You, Hashem our God, to see speedily the splendor of Your might, to remove idols from the earth, and the false gods shall be utterly cut off, to perfect the world under the kingship of the Almighty. “Let Mount Zion rejoice; let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of Your judgments.” “And of Zion it shall be said, ‘This man and that man was born in her,’ and the Most High Himself will establish her.” “Before Ephraim, Benjamin, and Manasseh, rouse Your might and come to save us.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the ninth day, the prince of the children of Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Abidan son of Gideoni, of the tribe of Benjamin, which is sealed with the point of Zion, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You took vengeance for the children of Israel upon the Egyptians, and went out to save Your people with Your great power — “Your right hand, Hashem, is glorious in power; Your right hand, Hashem, shatters the enemy”; “You stretched out Your right hand, the earth swallowed them” — in the merit of Benjamin the righteous, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, in this bitter and hasty exile, may Your hand find all Your enemies. “Your right hand will find those who hate You.” “The right hand of Hashem is exalted; the right hand of Hashem does valiantly.” “Look down from heaven and see, and visit this vine, the stock that Your right hand planted, and the son You made strong for Yourself.” “You will bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You made for Your dwelling, Hashem, the sanctuary, my Lord, that Your hands established,” in the portion of Benjamin, as it is said: “Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of Hashem shall dwell securely by Him; He covers him all day long, and dwells between his shoulders.” And He founded the foundation of Zion, in which You spent Your fury, and kindled a fire and consumed its foundations. Go forth now for the salvation of Your people, for the salvation of Your anointed; crush the head of the house of the wicked, laying bare the foundation up to the neck, Selah. “And of Zion it shall be said, ‘This man and that man was born in her,’ and the Most High Himself will establish her.” Unique and Exalted One, turn to Your people, who remember Your holiness. May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the tenth day, the prince of the children of Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, of the tribe of Dan, which is sealed with the lower segment of Splendor of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You stood by Your people Israel in their time of distress in the land of Egypt, and pleaded their cause and judged their case, in the merit of Dan, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, raise the horn of Messiah son of David, Your servant, whom You took from the seed of Dan, rulers together with the mother of David. “He shall judge among the nations, filling them with corpses; He shall crush the head over a vast land.” “He shall judge the poor with righteousness and decide with equity for the humble of the land; he shall strike the land with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips he shall slay the wicked.” “Rise up, Judge of the earth; render to the proud their recompense.” “To bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron, to execute upon them the judgment that is written.” “Saviors shall go up on Mount Zion to judge the mount of Esau, and the kingship shall be Hashem’s.” “For there thrones were set for judgment, thrones for the House of David.” “And Hashem will make His majestic voice heard, and will show the descent of His arm.” “Hashem, God of hosts, restore us; make Your face shine, that we may be saved.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the eleventh day, the prince of the children of Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ochran.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Pagiel son of Ochran, of the tribe of Asher, which is sealed with the attribute of the heel of Eternity of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You redeemed Your people, the House of Israel, from the iron furnace, from Egypt, in these days, at this time, and made a name for Yourself, as it is this day, and an ear heard and called them happy, saying, “Happy is the people for whom it is so,” in the merit of Asher, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, bring near for us the end of days of the redemption, and make with us a sign for good, a sign of salvation, and a sign of mercy. Let our enemies see and be ashamed; let our foes see and be put to shame, for You, Hashem, are our help and our comfort. “Then they said among the nations: ‘Hashem has done great things for them.’” “Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by Hashem?” “Happy is the nation whose God is Hashem, the people He has chosen as His inheritance.” And cause the horn of David, Your servant, to sprout, and prepare a lamp for the son of Jesse, Your anointed, speedily in our days. And as for Asher, in the land: “May he have dominion from sea to sea, and from the river to the ends of the earth. Before him the desert-dwellers shall bow, and his enemies shall lick the dust. The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall bring tribute; the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts. All kings shall bow down to him, all nations shall serve him. May his name endure forever; as long as the sun shines, may his name flourish; and all nations shall be blessed through him and call him happy.” “Hashem, God of hosts, restore us; make Your face shine, that we may be saved.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

On the twelfth day, the prince of the children of Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan. His offering was one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels by the sacred shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering; one gold ladle of ten shekels, filled with incense; one young bull, one ram, and one yearling lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and for the sacrifice of peace offerings, two oxen, five rams, five male goats, and five yearling lambs. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah of the order of the offering of the prince Ahira son of Enan, of the tribe of Naphtali, which is sealed with the attribute of the lower segment of Eternity of Kingship, his offering that he presented for the dedication of Your holy altar, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as when Israel went out from Egypt in these days, at this time, You chose us from among all the peoples and taught us Torah and commandments, sweeter than honey and the honeycomb, in the merit of Naphtali, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, sanctify us with Your commandments; set our portion in Your Torah in this present exile, so that it is never forgotten from the mouths of our seed. Make pleasant, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, the words of Your Torah in our mouths and in the mouths of Your people, the House of Israel. Place in our hearts understanding to understand and to discern, to hear, to learn and to teach, to keep, to do, and to fulfill all the words of the study of Your Torah in love. Enlighten our eyes in the study of Your Torah, and open our hearts to search and to explore in wisdom. “The riches of salvation are wisdom and knowledge,” so that they may be in our mouths like honey, “sweet to the soul and healing to the bone.” Have pity on Your people and have compassion on Your inheritance. “A shoot shall come out of the stump of Jesse, and a branch shall grow out of his roots; the spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and might, a spirit of knowledge and fear of Hashem.” “For out of Zion shall go forth Torah, and the word of Hashem from Jerusalem.” “God of hosts, turn again; look down from heaven and see, and visit this vine.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer. And afterward one says the prayer for the elevation of the souls.

Hashem spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and say to him: When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light toward the front of the menorah. Aaron did so; he set up its lamps toward the front of the menorah, as Hashem had commanded Moses. And this was the work of the menorah: hammered gold; from its base to its flowers it was hammered work; according to the pattern that Hashem showed Moses, so he made the menorah.

Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion, for behold, I am coming, and I will dwell in your midst, says Hashem. Many nations shall join themselves to Hashem on that day, and they shall be My people, and I will dwell in your midst; and you shall know that Hashem of hosts has sent me to you. Hashem will take possession of Judah as His portion on the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem. Be silent, all flesh, before Hashem, for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.

Then he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of Hashem, and the Adversary standing at his right hand to accuse him. Hashem said to the Adversary: Hashem rebuke you, Adversary; Hashem, who has chosen Jerusalem, rebuke you! Is this not a brand plucked from the fire? Now Joshua was clothed in filthy garments and was standing before the angel. The angel answered and said to those standing before him: Take the filthy garments off him. And to him he said: See, I have removed your iniquity from you, and I will clothe you in fine robes. And I said: Let them set a clean turban on his head. So they set a clean turban on his head and clothed him in garments, while the angel of Hashem stood by. Then the angel of Hashem charged Joshua: Thus says Hashem of hosts: If you walk in My ways and keep My charge, then you shall also govern My house and guard My courts, and I will give you free access among these who stand here. Hear now, Joshua the high priest, you and your companions who sit before you, for they are men of portent: behold, I am bringing My servant the Branch. For behold, the stone that I have set before Joshua, upon a single stone with seven eyes — behold, I will engrave its inscription, says Hashem of hosts, and I will remove the guilt of that land in a single day. On that day, says Hashem of hosts, you will invite one another under the vine and under the fig tree. The angel who spoke with me came back and woke me, like a man who is awakened from his sleep. He said to me: What do you see? I said: I see, and behold, a menorah all of gold, with a bowl on top of it, and its seven lamps upon it, seven spouts for each of the lamps that are on top of it. And two olive trees beside it, one on the right of the bowl and one on its left. I answered and said to the angel who spoke with me: What are these, my lord? The angel who spoke with me answered and said to me: Do you not know what these are? I said: No, my lord. He answered and said to me: This is the word of Hashem to Zerubbabel: Not by might and not by power, but by My spirit, says Hashem of hosts. Who are you, great mountain, before Zerubbabel? You shall become a plain! And he shall bring out the capstone with shouts of “Grace, grace to it!”

May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that our reading in the Torah, the reading of the portion of the lamps that You gave in love to Aaron, Your holy one, prince of the tribe of Levi, sealed with the Beauty of Kingship, be considered and accepted. May it be credited to us as though we had attained all the secrets and all the holy Names that come from the initial letters and final letters of these holy verses, and may we render the offerings of our lips in place of bulls. May there shine upon us, and upon all the House of Israel our brothers, all the sparks of holiness and all the holy lights that are contained in the holiness of this tribe. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, to understand and to gain insight in Your Torah and in Your awe, the awe of exaltation, to do Your will as Your will all the days of our lives, we and our children and our children’s children.

And just as You saw the affliction of Your people, the flock of Your pasture, in the iron furnace in Egypt, and joined them and accompanied them in all their distress, at the bush, in the merit of Levi, so, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, “I Am Who I Am” — Please, Mighty One, guard as the apple of Your eye those who seek Your unity, in this present exile; and in Your great goodness, let Your fierce anger turn away from Your people, from Your city, from Your land, and from Your inheritance. Fulfill for us the word that You promised us through Moses Your servant, saying: “I Am Who I Am.” “A help in times of trouble.” And it is said: “Even so, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them, to break My covenant with them, for I am Hashem their God.” And it is said: “In all their affliction He was afflicted, and the angel of His presence saved them; in His love and in His pity He redeemed them, and He lifted them and carried them all the days of old.” And return the priests to their service, and the Levites to their platform, and Israel to their station, and they shall accompany You and serve You.

And therefore we put our hope in You, Hashem our God, to see speedily the splendor of Your might. As it is said: “She will give to your head a garland of grace; a crown of beauty she will bestow on you.” “Awake, awake, put on your strength, O Zion; put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, the holy city.” “You shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of Hashem, and a royal diadem in the palm of your God.” And establish for Your people, the House of Israel, Your word, saying: “And to set you high above all the nations that He has made, for praise, for fame, and for glory.” “For You are the glory of their strength, and by Your favor our horn is exalted.” May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer.

segs.en: Various Blessings and Prayers
segs.text: ברכות ותפילות שונות

segs.en: Order of Betrothal
segs.text: סדר ארוסין
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן:

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ עַל הָעֲרָיוֹת וְאָסַר לָנוּ אֶת־הָאֲרוּסוֹת, וְהִתִּיר לָנוּ אֶת־הַנְּשׂוּאוֹת לָנוּ עַל יְדֵי חֻפָּה בְקִדּוּשִׁין. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, מְקַדֵּשׁ עַמּוֹ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל יְדֵי חֻפָּה בְקִדּוּשִׁין:

segs.en: The one who blessed drinks, and then the groom and the bride.
segs.text: <small>ושותה המברך ואחר כך החתן והכלה.</small>

segs.en: The groom says before giving the ring to the bride's finger:
segs.text: <small>החתן לפני שיתן הטבעת באצבע הכלה יאמר:</small>
הֲרֵי אַתְּ מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת לִי בְּטַבַּעַת זוֹ כְּדַת מֹשֶׁה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
“With your permission, my masters.” “To life!”
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the vine.

Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning forbidden relations, and forbade us the betrothed, and permitted us those who are married to us through the canopy and betrothal. Blessed are You, Hashem, who sanctifies His people Israel through the canopy and betrothal.
You are betrothed to me with this ring, according to the law of Moses and Israel.

segs.en: Order of the Seven Blessings
segs.text: סדר שבע ברכות
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהַכֹּל בָּרָא לִכְבוֹדוֹ:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, יוֹצֵר הָאָדָם:

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר יָצַר אֶת־הָאָדָם בְּצַלְמוֹ, בְּצֶלֶם דְמוּת תַּבְנִיתוֹ, וְהִתְקִין לוֹ מִמֶּנּוּ בִּנְיַן עֲדֵי־עַד. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, יוֹצֵר הָאָדָם:
שׂוֹשׂ תָּשִׂישׂ וְתָגֵל עֲקָרָה בְּקִבּוּץ בָּנֶיהָ לְתוֹכָהּ בִּמְהֵרָה בְּשִׂמְחָה. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, מְשַׂמֵּחַ צִיּוֹן בְּבָנֶיהָ:
שַׂמֵּחַ תְּשַׂמַּח רֵעִים אֲהוּבִים כְּשַׂמֵּחֲךָ יְצִירְךָ בְּגַן עֵדֶן מִקֶּדֶם. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, מְשַׂמֵּחַ חָתָן וְכַלָּה:

parts.text: מְהֵרָה יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ יִשָּׁמַע בְּעָרֵי יְהוּדָה וּבְחוּצוֹת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,

segs.en: And they taste the cup
segs.text: <small>וטועמים הכוס</small>

segs.en: And the groom breaks the cup in memory of Jerusalem
segs.text: <small>ושובר החתן כוס לזכרון ירושלם</small>

segs.en: And says:
segs.text: <small>ואומר:</small>
אִֽם־אֶשְׁכָּחֵ֥ךְ יְֽרוּשָׁלָ֗‍ִם תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח יְמִינִֽי׃ תִּדְבַּֽק־לְשׁוֹנִ֨י ׀ לְחִכִּי֮ אִם־לֹ֢א אֶ֫זְכְּרֵ֥כִי אִם־לֹ֣א אַ֭עֲלֶה אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֑‍ִם עַ֗֝ל רֹ֣אשׁ שִׂמְחָתִֽי׃
The person leading the blessings says, “With your permission, teachers and masters.” The guests answer, “To life!”
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who created everything for His glory.
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, Fashioner of humanity.

Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who fashioned the human being in His image, in the likeness of His form, and prepared from him an enduring structure. Blessed are You, Lord, Fashioner of humanity.
May barren Zion rejoice and be glad as her children are gathered to her in joy. Blessed are You, Lord, who gladdens Zion through her children.
Gladden these beloved companions as You gladdened Your creation in the Garden of Eden long ago. Blessed are You, Lord, who gladdens the groom and bride.

Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who created joy and gladness, groom and bride, rejoicing, song, delight and pleasure, love and fellowship, peace and friendship. May the voice of joy and gladness, the voice of groom and bride, the jubilant voices of grooms beneath their wedding canopies, and of youths at their feasts of song soon be heard in the cities of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem. Blessed are You, Lord, who gladdens the groom with the bride. (Some customs add: “and brings them joy.”)
They taste the cup.
The groom breaks a glass in remembrance of Jerusalem.
And he says:
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand wither. May my tongue cleave to my palate if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.

segs.en: Order of the Brit Milah
segs.text: סדר ברית מילה

segs.en: Prayer to be recited before the circumcision:
segs.text: <small>תפלה לאומרה לפני המילה:</small>

parts.text: לְיַחֲדָא שֵׁם יוֹד קֵ"י בְּוָא"ו קֵ"י בְּיִחוּדָא שְׁלִים בְּשֵׁם כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל. הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי בָּא לָמוּל תִּינוֹק זֶה

לְקַיֵּם מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: זֹ֣את בְּרִיתִ֞י אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּשְׁמְר֗וּ בֵּינִי֙ וּבֵ֣ינֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֵ֥ין זַרְעֲךָ֖ אַחֲרֶ֑יךָ הִמּ֥וֹל לָכֶ֖ם כׇּל־זָכָֽר׃ לְהַכְנִיסוֹ בִּבְרִיתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
וּלְהַכְנִיסוֹ בְּחוּלָקָא טָבָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,

דִּכְתִיב: וְ֝צַדִּ֗יק יְס֣וֹד עוֹלָֽם׃ וִיהֵא רַעֲוָא דְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּהַאי קָרְבָּנָא וְיִתְרְעִי בֵּיהּ. וְיִזְכֶּה לְעֶשֶׂר חֻפּוֹת רוּמִין שֶׁעָתִיד קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְמֶעְבַּד לְצַדִּיקַיָּא לְעַלְמָא דְּאָתִי,

כְּדִכְתִיב: אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ תִּ֥בְחַ֣ר וּתְקָרֵב֮ יִשְׁכֹּ֢ן חֲצֵ֫רֶ֥יךָ נִ֭שְׂבְּעָה בְּט֣וּב בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ קְ֝דֹ֗שׁ הֵיכָלֶֽךָ׃ וְעַתָּה בַּעֲוֹנוֹתֵינוּ חָֽרְבָה עִירֵנוּ וְשָׁמֵם בֵּית מִקְדָּשֵׁנוּ וְאֵין לָנוּ קָרְבָּנוֹת שֶׁיּכַפְּרוּ בַּעֲדֵנוּ. יְהִי רָצוֹן שֶׁיְּהֵא נֶחְשַׁב דַּם הַבְּרִית הַזֶּה כְּאִלּוּ בָּנִיתִי מִזְבֵּחַ וְהֶעֱלֵיתִי עָלָיו עוֹלוֹת וּזְבָחִים. יִֽהְי֥וּ לְרָצ֨וֹן ׀ אִמְרֵי־פִ֡י וְהֶגְי֣וֹן לִבִּ֣י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה צוּרִ֥י וְגֹאֲלִֽי׃ וִיהִ֤י ׀ נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ׃

segs.en: Prayer for the Sandek
segs.text: תפלה לסנדק

לְשֵׁם יִחוּד קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּהּ, בִּדְחִילוּ וּרְחִימוּ, וּרְחִימוּ וּדְחִילוּ, לְיַחֲדָא שֵׁם יוֹד קֵ"י בְּוָא"ו קֵ"י בְּיִחוּדָא שְׁלִים בְּשֵׁם כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל. הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי בָּא לִהְיוֹת סַנְדָּק וְאֶהְיֶה כִּסֵּא וּמִזְבֵּחַ לַעֲשׂוֹת עַל יְרֵכַי הַמִּילָה. וִיהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִזְבַּח כַּפָּרָה שֶׁתְּכַפֵּר עַל כָּל־חַטֹּאתַי, עֲוֹנוֹתַי וּפְשָׁעַי, וּבִפְרַט מַה שֶּׁפָּגַמְתִּי בִּירֵכַי וּבְאוֹת בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ. וְתַעֲלֶה עָלֵינוּ כְּאִלּוּ כִּוַּֽנְנוּ בְּכָל־הַכַּוָּנוֹת הָרְאוּיוֹת לְכַוֵּן, וּלְתַקֵּן אֶת־שָׁרְשָׁהּ בְּמָקוֹם עֶלְיוֹן, לַעֲשׂוֹת נַחַת רוּחַ לְיוֹצְרֵנוּ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן בּוֹרְאֵנוּ. וּתְמַלֵּא כָּל־הַשֵּׁמוֹת שֶּׁפָּגַֽמְתִּי בָּהֶם. וּתְהֵא הַמִּילָה חַשׁוּבָה כִּקְטֹרֶת סַמִּים, כְּדִכְתִיב גִּבְעַ֖ת הָעֲרָלֽוֹת, וּכְתִיב גִּבְעַ֖ת הַלְּבוֹנָֽה. וְיִתְקַיֵּם בָּֽנוּ מִקְרָא שֶׁכָּתוּב יָשִׂ֤ימוּ קְטוֹרָה֙ בְּאַפֶּ֔ךָ וְכָלִ֖יל עַֽל־מִזְבְּחֶֽךָ׃ בָּרֵ֤ךְ יְהֹוָה֙ חֵיל֔וֹ וּפֹ֥עַל יָדָ֖יו תִּרְצֶ֑ה. וִיהִ֤י ׀ נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ׃

segs.en: When the baby is brought to the synagogue, the entire congregation stands and says:
segs.text: <small>כשמביאים התינוק לבית הכנסת עומדים כל הקהל ואומרים</small>
בָּרוּךְ הַבָּא בְּשֵׁם יְהֹוָה:

segs.en: And when the father takes the baby in his hands, he says:
segs.text: <small>וכשלוקח אבי הבן את התינוק בידיו אומר</small>

שָׂ֣שׂ אָ֭נֹכִי עַל־אִמְרָתֶ֑ךָ כְּ֝מוֹצֵ֗א שָׁלָ֥ל רָֽב׃ זִ֥בְחֵ֣י אֱלֹהִים֮ ר֤וּחַ נִשְׁבָּ֫רָ֥ה לֵב־נִשְׁבָּ֥ר וְנִדְכֶּ֑ה אֱ֝לֹהִ֗ים לֹ֣א תִבְזֶֽה׃ הֵיטִ֣יבָה בִ֭רְצוֹנְךָ אֶת־צִיּ֑וֹן תִּ֝בְנֶ֗ה חוֹמ֥וֹת יְרוּשָׁלָֽ‍ִם׃ אָ֤ז תַּחְפֹּ֣ץ זִבְחֵי־צֶ֭דֶק עוֹלָ֣ה וְכָלִ֑יל אָ֤ז יַעֲל֖וּ עַל־מִזְבַּחֲךָ֣ פָרִֽים׃

segs.en: And then the father says:
segs.text: <small>ואחר כך יאמר אבי הבן</small>
אַשְׁרֵ֤י ׀ תִּ֥בְחַ֣ר וּתְקָרֵב֮ יִשְׁכֹּ֢ן חֲצֵ֫רֶ֥יךָ.

segs.en: And those standing answer:
segs.text: <small>ועונים העומדים</small>
נִ֭שְׂבְּעָה בְּט֣וּב בֵּיתֶ֑ךָ קְ֝דֹ֗שׁ הֵיכָלֶֽךָ׃

segs.en: In the Land of Israel it is customary to add these verses
segs.text: <small>בארץ ישראל נוהגים להוסיף פסוקים אלה</small>
אִֽם־אֶשְׁכָּחֵ֥ךְ יְֽרוּשָׁלָ֗‍ִם תִּשְׁכַּ֥ח יְמִינִֽי׃ תִּדְבַּֽק־לְשׁוֹנִ֨י ׀ לְחִכִּי֮ אִם־לֹ֢א אֶ֫זְכְּרֵ֥כִי אִם־לֹ֣א אַ֭עֲלֶה אֶת־יְרוּשָׁלַ֑‍ִם עַ֗֝ל רֹ֣אשׁ שִׂמְחָתִֽי׃

segs.en: And then he says
segs.text: <small>ואחר כך יאמר</small>
שְׁמַ֖ע יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל יְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ אֶחָֽד׃

parts.text: יְהֹוָה מָלָֽךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה ׀ יִמְלֹ֖ךְ לְעֹלָ֥ם וָעֶֽד:

parts.en: The father of the child says:
And the father of the child says:

segs.en: And blesses while standing
segs.text: <small>ומברך בעמידה</small>
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ לְהַכְנִיסוֹ בִּבְרִיתוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ:

segs.en: And the congregation and the mohel say:
segs.text: <small>והקהל והמוהל אומר:</small>
כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהִכְנַסְתּוֹ לַבְּרִית, כָּךְ תִּזְכֶּה לְהַכְנִיסוֹ לַתּוֹרָה וְלַמִּצְוֹת וְלַחֻפָּה וּלְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים:

segs.en: And the sandek sits on his chair. They place the infant on Elijah's chair, and say:
segs.text: <small>וישב הסנדק על הכסא שלו. ומניחים התינוק על כסא אליהו, ואומר</small>
זֶה הַכִּסֵּא שֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ הַנָּבִיא מַלְאַךְ הַבְּרִית זָכוּר לַטּוֹב:

segs.en: And the mohel takes the infant and places him on the sandek's lap, and before circumcising, blesses:
segs.text: <small>והמוהל יקבל התינוק ויניחו על ברכי הסנדק ולפני שימול יברך</small>
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ עַל הַמִּילָה:

segs.en: And after circumcising, the father of the child blesses:
segs.text: <small>ואחרי שימול יברך אבי הבן</small>
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהֶחֱיָֽינוּ וְקִיְּמָנוּ וְהִגִּיעָנוּ לַזְּמַן הַזֶּה:

segs.en: The mohel or another person takes a cup of wine and blesses:
segs.text: <small>ולוקח המוהל או אדם אחר כוס יין ומברך</small>
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּפֶן:

segs.en: Then he takes a myrtle branch and blesses:
segs.text: <small>ואחר כך לוקח הדס ומברך</small>
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, בּוֹרֵא עֲצֵי בְשָׂמִים:

בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר קִדֵּשׁ יְדִיד מִבֶּטֶן וְחוֹק בִּשְׁאֵרוֹ שָׂם, וְצֶאֱצָאָיו חָתַם בְּאוֹת בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ, עַל כֵּן בִּשְׂכַר זוֹ, אֵל חַי חֶלְקֵנוּ צוּרֵנוּ, צַוֵּה לְהַצִּיל יְדִידוּת זֶרַע קֹדֶשׁ שְׁאֵרֵנוּ מִשַּׁחַת, לְמַעַן בְּרִיתוֹ אֲשֶׁר שָׂם בִּבְשָׂרֵנוּ. בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, כּוֹרֵת הַבְּרִית:

parts.en: He tastes from the cup and says. When the father is the one blessing, he says the words in parentheses:
parts.text: <small>טועם מן הכוס ואומר. וכשהאב הוא מברך אומר הסוגרים</small>
וּלְאִמּוֹ וְיִקָּרֵא שְׁמוֹ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל (פְּלוֹנִי). יִשְׂמַח הָאִישׁ

וְתָגֵל הָאִשָּׁה בִּפְרִי בִטְנָהּ כָּאָמוּר: יִֽשְׂמַח־אָבִ֥יךָ וְאִמֶּ֑ךָ וְ֝תָגֵ֗ל יוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ׃ וְנֶאֱמַר: וָאֶעֱבֹ֤ר עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ וָֽאֶרְאֵ֔ךְ מִתְבּוֹסֶ֖סֶת בְּדָמָ֑יִךְ וָאֹ֤מַר לָךְ֙ בְּדָמַ֣יִךְ חֲיִ֔י

parts.en: He puts wine on his finger in the baby's mouth, and again the second time when he says 'and I said to you':
parts.text: <small>נותן יין באצבעו בפי התינוק, וכן בפעם השניה כשאומר ואומר לך</small>

וָאֹ֥מַר לָ֖ךְ בְּדָמַ֥יִךְ חֲיִֽי׃ וְנֶאֱמַר: זָכַ֣ר לְעוֹלָ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ דָּבָ֥ר צִ֝וָּ֗ה לְאֶ֣לֶף דּֽוֹר׃ אֲשֶׁ֣ר כָּ֭רַת אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וּשְׁב֖וּעָת֣וֹ לְיִשְׂחָֽק׃ וַיַּעֲמִידֶ֣הָ לְיַעֲקֹ֣ב לְחֹ֑ק לְ֝יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל בְּרִ֣ית עוֹלָֽם׃ הוֹד֣וּ לַיהֹוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃
כְּשֵׁם שֶׁנִּכְנַס לַבְּרִית כָּךְ יִכָּנֵס לַתּוֹרָה וְלַמִּצְוֹת וְלָחֻפָּה וּלְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים. וְכֵן יְהִי רָצוֹן וְנֹאמַר אָמֵן:

שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹת אַ֭שְׁרֵי כׇּל־יְרֵ֣א יְהֹוָ֑ה הַ֝הֹלֵ֗ךְ בִּדְרָכָֽיו׃ יְגִ֣יעַ כַּ֭פֶּיךָ כִּ֣י תֹאכֵ֑ל אַ֝שְׁרֶ֗יךָ וְט֣וֹב לָֽךְ׃ אֶשְׁתְּךָ ׀ כְּגֶ֥פֶן פֹּרִיָּה֮ בְּיַרְכְּתֵ֢י בֵ֫יתֶ֥ךָ בָּ֭נֶיךָ כִּשְׁתִלֵ֣י זֵיתִ֑ים סָ֝בִ֗יב לְשֻׁלְחָנֶֽךָ׃ הִנֵּ֣ה כִי־כֵ֭ן יְבֹ֥רַךְ גָּ֗בֶר יְרֵ֣א יְהֹוָֽה׃ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֗ה מִצִּ֫יּ֥וֹן וּ֭רְאֵה בְּט֣וּב יְרוּשָׁלָ֑‍ִם כֹּ֗֝ל יְמֵ֣י חַיֶּֽיךָ׃ וּרְאֵֽה־בָנִ֥ים לְבָנֶ֑יךָ שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

segs.en: And say Kaddish Yehe Shelama
segs.text: <small>ואומרים קדיש יהא שלמא</small>

For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, with fear and love, and love and fear, to unite the name Yod-Heh with Vav-Heh in perfect unity, in the name of all Israel: behold, I am coming to circumcise this child (the father says: to circumcise my son), to fulfill the positive commandment, as it is said: “This is My covenant, which you shall keep between Me and you and your descendants after you: every male among you shall be circumcised”; to bring him into the covenant of Abraham our father, and to bring him into the good portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: “The righteous one is the foundation of the world.” May it be the will of the Holy One, blessed be He, regarding this offering, and may He be pleased with it. And may he merit the ten lofty canopies that the Holy One, blessed be He, will make for the righteous in the World to Come, as it is written: “Happy is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts; we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your Temple.” And now, because of our sins our city has been laid waste and our Sanctuary is desolate, and we have no offerings to atone for us. May it be Your will that the blood of this covenant be considered as if I had built an altar and offered burnt offerings and sacrifices upon it. “May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Hashem, my Rock and my Redeemer.” “May the pleasantness of Hashem our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us, and the work of our hands, establish it.”

For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, with fear and love, and love and fear, to unite the name Yod-Heh with Vav-Heh in perfect unity, in the name of all Israel: behold, I am coming to be the sandek, and I will be a chair and an altar on which the circumcision is performed, upon my thighs. May it be Your will, Hashem our God and God of our fathers, that it be an altar of atonement that atones for all my sins, my iniquities and my transgressions, and especially for what I have damaged with my thighs and with the sign of the holy covenant. May it be counted for us as though we had intended all the proper intentions, and repair its root in the supreme place, to give contentment to our Maker and to do the will of our Creator. And restore all the Names that I have damaged through them. May the circumcision be considered like the incense of spices, as it is written, “the hill of the foreskins,” and it is written, “the hill of frankincense.” And may the verse that is written be fulfilled in us: “They shall put incense before You, and whole burnt offering on Your altar. Bless, Hashem, his substance, and accept the work of his hands.” “May the pleasantness of Hashem our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us, and the work of our hands, establish it.”
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of Hashem.

I rejoice at Your word, like one who finds great spoil. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, God, You will not despise. Do good to Zion in Your favor; build the walls of Jerusalem. Then You will delight in righteous sacrifices, in burnt offering and whole offering; then bulls will be offered upon Your altar.
Happy is the one You choose and bring near to dwell in Your courts.
We shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your Temple.
If I forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand wither. May my tongue cleave to my palate if I do not remember you, if I do not set Jerusalem above my highest joy.
Hear, O Israel: Hashem is our God, Hashem is One.
Hashem is King, Hashem has reigned, Hashem will reign forever and ever.
Please, Hashem, save us!
Please, Hashem, grant us success!
I appoint you as my agent to circumcise my son.
With the permission of my teachers and masters.
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to bring him into the covenant of Abraham our father.
Just as you have brought him into the covenant, so may you merit to bring him into the Torah, the commandments, the wedding canopy and good deeds.
This is the chair of Elijah the prophet, who is remembered for good, the angel of the covenant.
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning circumcision.
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this time.
“With your permission, my masters.” “To life!”
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the vine.
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who creates fragrant trees.

Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, who sanctified the beloved one from the womb, set a statute in his flesh, and sealed his descendants with the sign of the holy covenant. Therefore, as reward for this, living God, our Portion, our Rock, command that the beloved of our flesh be saved from destruction, for the sake of His covenant that He set in our flesh. Blessed are You, Hashem, who makes the covenant.

Our God and God of our fathers, sustain this child for his father (for me) and for his mother, and let his name in Israel be called (so-and-so). Let the man rejoice (May it be Your will that I rejoice in the offspring of my loins) in the offspring of his loins, and let the woman be glad in the fruit of her womb, as it is said: “Let your father and your mother rejoice, and let she who bore you be glad.” And it is said: “I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, and I said to you: In your blood, live! And I said to you: In your blood, live!” And it is said: “He remembered His covenant forever, the word He commanded for a thousand generations, which He made with Abraham and swore to Isaac. He established it for Jacob as a statute, for Israel as an everlasting covenant.” “Give thanks to Hashem, for He is good, for His kindness endures forever.” This little one, may God make him great. Just as he has entered the covenant, so may he enter the Torah, the commandments, the wedding canopy and good deeds. And so may it be His will, and let us say: Amen.

A song of ascents. Happy is everyone who fears Hashem, who walks in His ways. When you eat the labor of your hands, you shall be happy, and it shall be well with you. Your wife shall be like a fruitful vine in the innermost parts of your house; your children like olive saplings around your table. Behold, so shall the man be blessed who fears Hashem. May Hashem bless you from Zion, and may you see the good of Jerusalem all the days of your life. And may you see children of your children. Peace upon Israel.

leaves.path: Assorted Blessings and Prayers/Redeeming the First Born
leaves.title: סדר פדיון הבן

segs.en: Order of Redeeming the First Born
segs.text: סדר פדיון הבן

segs.en: The kohen takes the child and asks the father:
segs.text: <small>לוקח הכהן את הילד ושואל לאביו</small>

parts.en: And the kohen says to him:

parts.text: בְּבִנְךָ בְכוֹרֶךָ אוֹ בְחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים דִּמְחַיַּבְתְּ לִפְדּוֹת בָּהֶן?

parts.en: Then the kohen asks the mother of the child:

parts.text: בְּנֵךְ זֶה בְּכוֹר. שֶׁמֶּא יָלַדְתְּ בֵּן אַחֵר לְפָנָיו אוֹ שֶׁמֶּא הִפַּלְתְּ?
זֶה בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי לֹא יָלַדְתִּי וְלֹא הִפַּלְתִּי לְפָנָיו:

שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: וּפְדוּיָו֙ מִבֶּן־חֹ֣דֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּ֔ה בְּעֶ֨רְכְּךָ֔ כֶּ֛סֶף חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת שְׁקָלִ֖ים בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים גֵּרָ֖ה הֽוּא׃ כְּשֶׁהָיִיתָ בִּמְעֵי אִמֶּךָ הָיִיתָ בִּרְשׁוּת אָבִיךָ שֶׁבַּשָּׁמַיִם וּבִרְשׁוּת אָבִיךָ וְאִמֶּךָ. עַכְשָׁיו אַתָּה בִּרְשׁוּתִי שֶׁאֲנִי כֹהֵן וְאָבִיךָ וְאִמֶּךָ מְבַקְּשִׁים לִפְדּוֹתְךָ שֶׁאַתָּה בְּכוֹר מְקֻדָּשׁ,
שֶׁכֵּן כָּתוּב: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ קַדֶּשׁ־לִ֨י כׇל־בְּכ֜וֹר פֶּ֤טֶר כׇּל־רֶ֙חֶם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לִ֖י הֽוּא׃

segs.en: Then the father takes the silver or its value in his hand and says:
segs.text: <small>אחר כך יטול האב את הכסף או שוה כסף בידו ויאמר</small>

אֲנִי רוֹצֶה לִפְדּוֹתוֹ שֶׁכָּךְ כָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה: אַ֣ךְ ׀ פָּדֹ֣ה תִפְדֶּ֗ה אֵ֚ת בְּכ֣וֹר הָֽאָדָ֔ם: וּפְדוּיָו֙ מִבֶּן־חֹ֣דֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּ֔ה בְּעֶ֨רְכְּךָ֔ כֶּ֛סֶף חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת שְׁקָלִ֖ים בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים גֵּרָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

segs.en: Before the blessing he says for the sake of the unification:
segs.text: <small>לפני הברכה יאמר לשם יחוד</small>

לְשֵׁם יִחוּד קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ, בִּדְחִֽילוּ וּרְחִֽימוּ, וּרְחִֽימוּ וּדְחִֽילוּ, לְיַחֲדָא שֵׁם יוֹ"ד קֵ"א בְּוָא"ו קֵ"א בְּיִחוּדָא שְׁלִים, בְּשֵׁם כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵל. הִנֵּה אָנֹכִי בָּא לְקַיֵּם מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁל פִּדְיוֹן בְּכוֹר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: וְכֹ֨ל בְּכ֥וֹר אָדָ֛ם בְּבָנֶ֖יךָ תִּפְדֶּֽה׃ וּכְתִיב: וּפְדוּיָו֙ מִבֶּן־חֹ֣דֶשׁ תִּפְדֶּ֔ה בְּעֶ֨רְכְּךָ֔ כֶּ֛סֶף חֲמֵ֥שֶׁת שְׁקָלִ֖ים בְּשֶׁ֣קֶל הַקֹּ֑דֶשׁ עֶשְׂרִ֥ים גֵּרָ֖ה הֽוּא׃ וְיַעֲלֶה לְפָנֶיךָ כְּאִלּוּ קִיַּמְתִּיהָ בְּכָל־פְּרָטֶיהָ וְדִקְדּוּקֶיהָ וְכַוָּנוֹתֶיהָ וְתַרְיַ"ג מִצְוֹת הַתְּלוּיוֹת בָּהּ וּלְתַקֵּן אֶת־שָׁרְשָׁהּ בְּמָקוֹם עֶלְיוֹן, לַעֲשׂוֹת נַחַת רוּחַ לְיוֹצְרֵנוּ וְלַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹן בּוֹרְאֵנוּ. וִיהִ֤י ׀ נֹ֤עַם אֲדֹנָ֥י אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ עָ֫לֵ֥ינוּ וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יָ֭דֵינוּ כּוֹנְנָ֥ה עָלֵ֑ינוּ וּֽמַעֲשֵׂ֥ה יָ֝דֵ֗ינוּ כּוֹנְנֵֽהוּ:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ עַל פִּדְיוֹן הַבֵּן:
בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, שֶׁהֶחֱיָֽינוּ וְקִיְּמָנוּ וְהִגִּיעָנוּ לַזְּמַן הַזֶּה:

segs.en: He gives it to the kohen and says:
segs.text: <small>יתן לכהן ויאמר</small>
זֶה פִּדְיוֹן בְּנִי בְכוֹרִי:

segs.en: And the kohen takes the silver and says:
segs.text: <small>ויקבל הכהן את הכסף ויאמר</small>
קִבַּלְתִּי מִמְּךָ חֲמִשָּׁה סְלָעִים אֵֽלּוּ בְּפִדְיוֹן בִּנְךָ זֶה, וַהֲרֵי הוּא פָּדוּי בָּהֶן כְּדַת מֹשֶׁה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל:

parts.en: It is customary that the kohen blesses the child

parts.text:
וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהֹוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־בָּנָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה תְבָרְכ֖וּ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָמ֖וֹר לָהֶֽם׃ יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה וְיִשְׁמְרֶֽךָ׃ יָאֵ֨ר יְהֹוָ֧ה ׀ פָּנָ֛יו אֵלֶ֖יךָ וִֽיחֻנֶּֽךָּ׃ יִשָּׂ֨א יְהֹוָ֤ה ׀ פָּנָיו֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם׃ וְשָׂמ֥וּ אֶת־שְׁמִ֖י עַל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַאֲנִ֖י אֲבָרְכֵֽם׃

יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ,
וּלְמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים בְּחַיֵּי אָבִיו וּבְחַיֵּי אִמּוֹ,

segs.text: Is this son of yours a firstborn? Yes. Which do you want more: your firstborn son, or the five selas that you are obliged to give to redeem him? My firstborn son. Is this son of yours a firstborn? Have you perhaps borne another son before him, or have you perhaps miscarried? This is my firstborn son; I have not borne a child before him, and I have not miscarried.
